title: Dutch
description: Everyday Dutch: greetings, family, food, numbers, getting around and your day.

units.title: Greetings
units.description: Say hello, introduce yourself and be polite.
units.tip: 'Dank je' and 'alsjeblieft' are informal; 'dank u' and 'alstublieft' are polite. 'Dag' can mean hello or goodbye.

units.title: People and family
units.description: Talk about the people around you.
units.tip: Dutch has two words for 'the': 'de' for most nouns and 'het' for others, such as 'het kind' (the child).

units.title: Food and drink
units.tip: 'Geen' means 'no / not any': 'Ik drink geen melk' = I do not drink milk.

units.title: Numbers
units.description: Count from one to ten, ask prices and tell the time.
units.tip: Write 'één' with accents when you mean the number one, to tell it apart from 'een' (a / an).

units.title: Travel and directions
units.description: Find your way around a new city.
units.tip: 'Linksaf' and 'rechtsaf' are for turning left and right; 'links' and 'rechts' mean on the left and on the right.

exercises.prompt: The station is on the right.

exercises.translation: The station is on the right.

answers: I am going to the airport.

options: I am going to the airport.

exercises.translation: I am going to the airport.

exercises.prompt: I am going to the airport.

accepted: The station is to the right.
The station is on your right.

units.title: Daily routine
units.description: Home, work, school and the time of day.
units.tip: ''s Ochtends' (in the morning) and ''s nachts' (at night) start with an apostrophe and a small s.

exercises.prompt: I drink coffee in the morning.

exercises.translation: I drink coffee in the morning.

answers: The children are going to school.

accepted: In the morning I drink coffee.
In the morning, I drink coffee.
